films.title: Why fund data needs a standard
films.description: Why the fund industry needs a common data format: how fund data travels between asset managers, administrators, custodians, distributors, insurers, data vendors and regulators; what goes wrong without a standard; how regulation drives the need for structured data; and how FundsXML, an open standard made by the fund industry, answers it.

films.title: What a FundsXML delivery contains
films.description: What a FundsXML delivery carries, in business terms: fund and share class master data, net asset values and prices, portfolios and holdings, transactions and distributions, documents, country modules and regulatory data. Why static and dynamic data are kept apart, typical kinds of deliveries, and a look into a real file, including a ready-made query for the largest holdings.

films.title: Regulatory reporting with FundsXML
films.description: How FundsXML carries the European regulatory templates: why regulation needs structured fund data, the roles of FinDatEx and FundsXML, the templates EMT (MiFID II), EPT (PRIIPs), EET (SFDR and ESG), TPT (Solvency II look-through) and EFT (feedback from distributors), who sends what to whom, template versions, national reporting and the European Single Access Point.

films.title: Trust in the data: quality and control
films.description: How the quality of fund data is secured with FundsXML: why a valid file is not yet correct data, the three levels readable, valid and plausible, what the schema checks and what business rules check, check digits of identifiers, checks on both sides, corrections and versions, and a data-quality report in FreeXmlToolkit.

films.title: Introducing FundsXML: a project from A to Z
films.description: How a FundsXML project runs, from the first idea to daily operation: scope, mapping, prototype and pilot, testing, go-live and operations; the roles involved, typical pitfalls, what is available free of charge, how versions and the standard evolve, and how to take part.

films.title: Taking part in FundsXML
films.description: How FundsXML evolves and how to take part: the FundsXML Standards Committee, the secretariat and the three working groups (Content & Technique, Promotion, Documentation), associate and full membership, contributing on GitHub, the path of a change request from proposal to a new version, small and large changes, and what makes a good change request.

films.title: Set up FreeXmlToolkit for FundsXML
films.description: Set up a free working environment for FundsXML: turn on the FundsXML extension of FreeXmlToolkit, choose the schema version, get to know the FundsXML panel and its tools, read the schema's documentation of any element, open the schema itself, and start from an official example file. Also: why FundsXML needs an XSD 1.1 validator, and the two forms in which the schema is published. With an overview of other tools: command line validators, IDEs and the online documentation.

films.title: Anatomy of a delivery: structure and ControlData
films.description: How a FundsXML document is built: the root element FundsXML4, its main blocks (ControlData, Funds, AssetMasterData, Documents, RegulatoryReportings, CountrySpecificData), and ControlData in detail: document ID, timestamps, schema version, content date, data supplier, and the data operations INITIAL, AMEND and DELETE with related document IDs. With common pitfalls. Includes turning a delivery into a correction in FreeXmlToolkit.

films.title: Funds, share classes and NAV
films.description: The fund part of a FundsXML document: fund identifiers and names, SingleFundFlag with single funds and umbrellas, FundStaticData and FundDynamicData, the total net asset value, share classes with prices, shares outstanding and amounts in several currencies (AmountType with ccy), action codes, and checking ISIN and LEI check digits in FreeXmlToolkit.

films.title: Portfolios and asset master data
films.description: The portfolio part of a FundsXML document: positions with their value and weight, the instrument-specific block (equities, bonds, fund units, options, FX forwards, cash), the link from a position to its asset in AssetMasterData through UniqueID (xs:ID and xs:IDREF), a broken link found by the schema, portfolio breakdowns, and how fund-of-fund look-through is modelled.

films.title: Transactions and investor flows
films.description: How FundsXML records what moved in a fund: subscriptions and redemptions of investors (Flows on the share class), distributions (Distributions), income from the portfolio (Earnings) and the portfolio's own trades (Transactions), with reporting periods, dates, amounts in several currencies and the links to the assets. Also: how switches are reported, and what the core schema leaves to other standards.

films.title: Regulatory templates in XML
films.description: How the FinDatEx templates sit in a FundsXML file: RegulatoryReportings with DirectReporting and IndirectReporting, an EMT V4.2 block (data set information, general information, target market, ex-ante costs) and a TPT V7 block for Solvency II (portfolio data, positions with CIC codes and valuations), template versions as their own elements, and how country-specific data and custom attributes extend the standard.

films.title: Documents: link, embed, extract
films.description: How FundsXML carries documents such as prospectuses, PRIIPs KIDs and factsheets: the Documents block, document types, languages and countries, the assignment to funds and share classes, format, signature and dates, delivery as a link or embedded as base64, replacing and restricted documents, and the Documents tool of FreeXmlToolkit to save embedded documents and embed new ones.

films.title: Validate and check data quality
films.description: Validate a FundsXML delivery in two stages: against the XSD 1.1 schema, reading and fixing its error messages, and against business rules with the FundsXML data-quality checks of FreeXmlToolkit. With the data-quality report, a catalogue of typical schema errors, Schematron rules, and validation on the command line and in build pipelines.

films.title: Query, transform and integrate
films.description: Work with the data in a FundsXML file: XPath paths without a namespace, the ready-made FundsXML queries in the Query Console of FreeXmlToolkit (the ten largest positions as a table), an XSLT stylesheet that turns the positions into CSV, strategies for large files, and how FundsXML fits into a system landscape of databases, data warehouses and scheduled deliveries.

films.title: A FundsXML delivery chain
films.description: How FundsXML runs in production: who sends what to whom, the delivery chain of sender and receiver, data sources and a central database, how files travel (SFTP, API, portals), security, rhythms and schema versions, roles, the five building blocks of a production setup, build or buy, how to start, and the complete example used in this series, which can be downloaded.

films.title: FundsXML in a database
films.description: How FundsXML data is stored in a database, with the complete PostgreSQL example of the FundsXML examples repository: the XML column and shredded tables, layers, a table model in which everything that repeats is a row (several funds per file, umbrellas and subfunds, several NAVs per day and currency, portfolios and positions, look-through), keys and assets without an ISIN, amounts and currencies, code lists, dates, transactions in four places, documents, regulatory templates, history and corrections, views, quality, access and performance. All files can be downloaded.

films.title: Loading FundsXML files
films.description: How FundsXML files get into a database safely, with the loader of the complete PostgreSQL example: the steps of a robust loader, a landing folder, cheap checks first, triggers, validation and schema versions, idempotency through the UniqueDocumentID, full and delta deliveries, streaming large files with one handler per repeating element, funds and subfunds, the order of assets and positions, asset keys, transactions, documents and regulatory templates, business rules, speed, six deliveries and four broken files at work, corrections and deletions, reconciliation, code checks, error reports, tests and release. All files can be downloaded.

films.title: Generating FundsXML
films.description: How to produce FundsXML from a database, with the generator of the complete PostgreSQL example: start with the target file, a mapping table, a partner register that says which data goes to whom, templates, XSLT or generated code, ControlData, writing share classes, several funds and dates in one file, element order, empty elements and formats, validation in FreeXmlToolkit, corrections, large deliveries, several schema versions, partner configuration, time windows, golden files, CI and the round trip, handing over, resends and documentation. All files can be downloaded.

films.title: Running FundsXML in daily operations
films.description: What daily operation of a FundsXML chain needs: a day in operations, monitoring and a delivery overview, duty and runbooks, error classes and incident handling with an example, reconciliation, feedback, agreements with partners, onboarding, changes in the partner landscape, security, schema upgrades, the archive, metrics, people, reporting, typical first-year issues, a checklist, and staying involved in the standard.

disclaimer: Disclaimer: This video is for training purposes only and is not legal, regulatory or investment advice.
